title: Lot Lines, Easements & Setbacks
description: Basic concepts of lots, lot lines, easements, setbacks, privacy easements, courts and yards, and allowable building areas used in architectural site planning.

content.text: A lot is a defined parcel of land on which a building or other development may be located. The lot is identified by its boundaries and dimensions.

items: A lot is a parcel of land.
Its boundaries define the extent of the property.
The building location must be planned within the lot.

content.text: A lot line is a boundary line that defines the limits of a property or lot.

items: Front lot line
Rear lot line
Side lot lines
Lot lines define the property boundaries.

content.text: An easement is a legal right affecting the use of land. It may provide a person or property with a specific right to use part of another property for a particular purpose.

items: Easements may affect how a property can be developed.
An easement can restrict construction within a particular area.
The purpose of an easement determines how the affected area may be used.

content.text: A setback is the required distance between a building and a property boundary, road, or other reference line. Setbacks provide required open spaces around buildings.

items: Front setback
Side setback
Rear setback
Setbacks help regulate building placement.

content.text: Certain privacy-related easements may require a minimum distance between structures and property boundaries. A two-meter distance is associated with specific privacy easement provisions.

items: Privacy easements can limit the placement of openings.
The required distance protects privacy between adjoining properties.
The applicable legal provision should be checked for the specific situation.

content.text: Courts, yards, and setbacks provide open spaces around buildings. These spaces contribute to light, ventilation, access, and safe building planning.

items: Courts provide open spaces within or around building arrangements.
Yards provide required open spaces around buildings.
Setbacks control how close a building can be placed to property boundaries.

content.text: The allowable building area is affected by lot dimensions, required setbacks, easements, and other applicable regulations. Site planning must account for these restrictions before determining the building footprint.

items: Determine lot boundaries.
Identify required setbacks.
Identify applicable easements.
Determine the area available for the building.
Check applicable building regulations.
